verdicts.tldr: the gnoalias.sh route the README recommends for several hosts restarts gnoweb on every host each time the block changes, the request drop the README warns against
verdicts.details: README.md:85-87 warns that restarting gnoweb with ON_CHANGE on several hosts makes every host drop requests for the same post, then line 91 sends multi-host setups through gnoalias.sh writing home-override.md. gnoalias.sh copies home-override.md over home.md whenever cmp differs and then runs RELOAD_CMD, which by default is docker restart of every gnoweb:master container, so each block change restarts gnoweb on every host within a 60 s poll. #6327, which would let gnoweb re-read the page, is still OPEN. How many restarts a day this costs was not measured here. Fix: say in the README that the gnoalias route restarts gnoweb on each change until #6327 lands, or hold that route until then.

verdicts.verify_by: STATE_DIR=$(mktemp -d) bash misc/deployments/home-alias/whatsnew.sh --source x | grep -c 'CompleteGno'; and curl publish.x.com/oembed for that status to see the missing break
verdicts.tldr: the mainnet home's X post reads 'CompleteGno.land' because tag stripping glues the word before a link to the link's replacement
verdicts.details:
X's oEmbed html for status 2123072056153759774 has no space or
between 'Complete' and the tag, where the post had a line break. html_to_text removes the tag, leaving 'Completehttps://t.co/UPaevcA79z', and expand_links swaps that t.co URL for 'Gno.land' since it redirects to https://gno.land/, so visitors read 'Upgrade: CompleteGno.land mainnet is now running v1.8.0'. Fix: replace each opening tag with a space before stripping tags, e.g. gsub("]*>"; " "), so the later space squeeze keeps one blank.

verdicts.verify_by: extract the block as line 225 does, then `bash -c 'source block.sh; source block.sh'` with gnokey and gno stubbed; ls myrealm/myrealm
verdicts.tldr: the 'second run' test re-runs the block from a fresh shell, while a reader who re-pastes it in the same terminal is already inside myrealm/ and gets myrealm/myrealm/
verdicts.details: Both runs at lines 226 and 233 start with `cd "$work/deploy"` in a new subshell, so the check can only catch a missing -p on mkdir. The block does `mkdir -p myrealm && cd myrealm`, and in a real terminal that cd persists, so a re-paste after fixing <your-g1-addr> writes into myrealm/myrealm/; the check's name says a second run still writes into myrealm/. The double-source run was not done; the shell semantics follow from the lines. Fix: run the second paste from inside myrealm/ in the test, and make the block safe to re-paste, e.g. `[ "${PWD##*/}" = myrealm ] || { mkdir -p myrealm && cd myrealm; }`, or rename the check to what it covers.
